citation.authors: Shamsutdinova D, Stahl D, Das-Munshi J

cited_by.title: Type 2 diabetes risk and blood sugar

record.population: About 340,000 adults without diabetes in South London primary care, followed 2012-2019
record.design: Cohort study with Cox models, adjusted stepwise for age, sex, migration, mental health, BMI, blood pressure and deprivation
record.finding: South Asian, Black African and Black Caribbean groups had 2 to 3 times the type 2 diabetes risk of White British people, which was only partly explained by socioeconomic and clinical factors. Being born outside the UK raised risk by 29% across all groups. Depression, anxiety and severe mental illness were also linked to higher risk.
record.note: One region of London; ethnic group is the recorded category in GP records. Funding not checked.
